---
title: "Accuracy and availability: airports worldwide"
description: "The 100 airports with the most movements in OPDI's flight list: how often each main item exists there. Outside Europe there is no reference, so this is availability, not accuracy."
---

**Outside Europe this page shows how often an item is found, not whether it
is correct.** There are no airport records outside Europe, and Network
Manager knows only the flights to and from Europe, so nothing confirms a
take-off time or a stand at an airport in the United States or in Asia. An
item found there may still be wrong.

The airports are the 100 with the most departures and arrivals in OPDI's
own flight list on the three days measured (10, 14 and 17 June 2026).
Of them, 70 are outside Europe and 30 in
Europe, 28 of which send airport records. For the accuracy at the
European airports, see [the European airport page](europe.qmd); the
references and the labels are explained on
[Accuracy and availability](index.qmd).

## How to read this page

Each cell of the table below gives, for one item at one airport, the share
of OPDI's flights at the airport that carry it (the departures for
departure items, the arrivals for arrival items) and its label: `high` at
least 80 %, `partial` 50 % to under 80 %, `low` under 50 %. The column
"Reference" says what can be checked at the airport. The ranking follows
OPDI's own flights, so it favours the regions where OpenSky has many
receivers.

A low share at an airport means that the item is mostly missing there,
for example because the receivers around the airport do not hear aircraft low
down or on the ground. A high share says only that the item exists.

## Per item {#per-item}

Each table gives, for one item, the share and the count it is computed
over, and, where a reference exists, the accuracy. Outside Europe the
departure and destination airports are compared with Network Manager only
for the flights to and from Europe; the other items have no reference
there. Open a table to see it.
